summary: The law you signed, and the backlash: Days after you sign {the law}, {employer} says it will take its jobs or its event elsewhere, and your own backers say any change is a betrayal.
realLife: One life: In 2015 he signed an Indiana religious-objections law that businesses and conventions called anti-gay. He said on television the law would not change, then signed a revision days later; a company canceled a planned expansion, and backers of the original were angry. The same year he let counties open needle exchanges during an HIV outbreak, which he had opposed. Another: In 2006 the Louisiana governor signed a ban on most abortions to take effect if the Supreme Court allowed it. She thought exceptions for rape and incest were reasonable but felt she should not veto it.
gates: An employer or group on record has said it will pull out, cancel or protest over it.
weights: How many jobs {employer} holds in the place.
